title: Author and narrator
statement: Literary analysis distinguishes the historical author from the narrator or speaking voice constructed within a text, so a narrator's statements are not automatically the author's factual commitments.
limitations: Some works deliberately blur these roles, and interpretations should be supported by textual and historical evidence.

title: Poetic meter
statement: Meter is an organized pattern of rhythmic units in verse; its realization depends on the language, poetic tradition, and relation between abstract pattern and performed stress, duration, or syllable weight.
limitations: Not all poetry is metrical, and the same line may admit more than one defensible scansion.

title: The ghost's accusation in Hamlet
statement: Within Shakespeare's Hamlet, the ghost appearing to Hamlet identifies itself as his dead father and accuses Claudius of murder, initiating a claim that drives the play's investigation and revenge plot.
limitations: This is a statement about events and assertions inside a fictional drama, not historical evidence of a real murder or apparition.

title: Revision separates generation from evaluation
statement: A useful writing practice is to separate initial generation from later evaluation, then revise for purpose, structure, evidence, clarity, rhythm, and correctness in distinct passes when the task benefits from it.
limitations: This is a craft heuristic rather than a universal law; some writers compose and revise recursively or simultaneously.

title: Scene and summary control narrative time
statement: Writers can vary narrative pace by rendering events as scenes with moment-to-moment action or compressing longer spans into summary, choosing the balance according to emphasis, rhythm, and reader orientation.
limitations: Scene is not inherently superior to summary; both are tools whose effect depends on context and execution.

title: Claims need proportionate support
statement: Expository and argumentative writing is stronger when the scope and certainty of a claim are proportionate to the quality, relevance, and limitations of the evidence offered for it.
limitations: Standards of support vary by genre, audience, discipline, and purpose; creative writing may use different truth conventions.
